title: Steps inside a stage: a run records what it did, one entry at a time, with a digest of what each produced
request: Phase 1's gap: a stage's run record said what it read and what it made, not how it got there; a decision could not be traced to the exact numbers it was made on, and a replay that diverged could not say where. One entry per transform, fold, fit, prediction and metric, with shapes, parameters, the fold, the metric and its value, the time and a digest; adoptable by the main product.
spec: dclab_core.steps (Step, collect, step, digest_of, compare; free when nothing collects); RunRecord v2 with steps; the events pipeline.step_started and pipeline.step_finished; the runner and the engine record the recipe fit and transform, model fit, prediction, fold and fold metric, the split, the holdout metrics and interval; GET /api/projects/{id}/steps?stage= or ?decision=; a replay reports same_steps and the first step whose digest differs; the adapter reads the main product's fold and candidate rows as steps.
plan: The contract and the recorder in dclab_core as a context that costs nothing when nothing collects, so library code can call it freely.
A digest of what a step produced: bounded, rounded, deterministic, keeping no value.
Instrument the runner's fit_and_predict and cross_validate and the engine's data and final stages; collect in the engine's run wrapper; put the steps in the stage's run record.
Two events per step under the run; the route and the decision trace; the replay's comparison.
The adapter for the main product's rows that already are steps.

decisions.decision: A step's index is where it began; the log keeps steps in that order though an outer fold ends after its inner steps.
decisions.why: A reader and a replay compare by position: the order must be the order of the work, not the order of the endings.

decisions.decision: A digest reads at most 5000 rows and 200 columns, rounded to six decimals, with the shape.
decisions.why: A faithful rerun must give the same digest on any machine, and hashing a whole matrix per fold would cost more than the fold.

decisions.decision: At most 600 steps per run; the rest are counted.
decisions.why: A models stage runs six families, two optimisations and folds; the record must stay readable and small.

decisions.decision: Step is defined with the run record it belongs to.
decisions.why: steps imports the contract base and the contract base imports lineage: putting Step in lineage keeps the import order one-way.

decisions.decision: A kind's machine is one step.
decisions.why: Its internals are not instrumented; the stage still shows that a machine ran, and what it produced is the stage record.

change: dclab_core steps.py (new), lineage.py (Step, RunRecord v2, compare, event payload), experience.py (the step kinds, run.recorded steps), adapters/main_product_experience.py (steps_from_run_events), CHANGELOG 0.46.0, schemas; dclab_rnd expansion/runner.py, studio/engine.py, studio/lineage.py (stage_steps, decision_steps, runs), agentic/routers/projects.py (the steps route), experience/__main__.py (replay fails on a step difference); tests test_steps.py (new), test_experience_log; CORE_INTEGRATION.md, the plan.

findings.defect: Steps were listed in the order they ended, so a fold came after the fit inside it and a position-by-position comparison pinned the wrong step.
findings.scenario: A replay with step 2's digest changed reported position 1.
findings.cause: The index was taken at the start, the list appended at the end.
findings.fix: A slot is reserved when a step begins and filled when it ends.

findings.defect: steps imported the contract base, which imports lineage, which imports steps.
findings.scenario: import dclab_rnd.expansion.runner failed in a fresh interpreter.
findings.cause: A cycle that only shows when steps is imported first.

findings.defect: The run event did not know about steps and refused the new count.
findings.scenario: run.recorded refused: fields not in the vocabulary: ['steps'].
findings.cause: event_payload gained a field the vocabulary lacks.
findings.fix: steps is a count of run.recorded.

findings.defect: test_experience_log lists every event of the main flow; the step events are many.
findings.scenario: The expected sequence failed with pipeline.step_started inside it.
findings.cause: A new kind in the flow.
findings.fix: The flow test leaves pipeline.step_* out; test_steps counts them.

findings.defect: The pipeline rerun route dropped every step result.
findings.scenario: POST .../pipeline/rerun?step=stage:models after a change in one fold's predictions answered with same_numbers only; the step walk reached only make replay.
findings.cause: The job logs a fixed key list and the route answers from the logged payload.
findings.fix: same_steps, first_step_difference and steps_compared are in the list; a test runs the handler with a replay that differs.

findings.defect: A change in a metric, or past row 5000, was never pinned to a step: compare ignored the value, fit/fold/metric steps had no digest, and a digest read only the first 5000 rows.
findings.scenario: Two metric steps of 0.81 and 0.55 compared identical; two 20,000-element arrays differing at index 15,000 had equal digests.
findings.cause: Digests existed only for arrays and read a bounded sample.
findings.fix: A metric step is digested by its value; an array digest adds a checksum of the whole array and the sample is rounded to six decimals with signed zero normalised; the bootstrap interval is digested as an array.

findings.defect: A decision did not trace cleanly: metric steps carried no candidate, and a decision of a stage that ran again returned nothing.
findings.scenario: 54 steps for a models decision with the candidate recoverable only by position; a superseded run returned steps [].
findings.cause: The config id was only in the fold step, which the decision view filtered out; the superseded run was only read from the stage record.
findings.fix: The metric step names its candidate; a superseded run's steps are read from its pipeline.step_finished events.

findings.defect: The package text asked for imputation and encoding as steps; a recipe is one transform step.
findings.scenario: No clean, impute, encode or select step is ever emitted.
findings.cause: The frame recipe is one object.
findings.fix: Said in CORE_INTEGRATION and the status as a limit of the granularity.

findings.defect: A step's own failure could change a run: Step refuses nan and inf, digest_of raises on some sparse formats, the Step build in finally replaced the body's exception.
findings.scenario: A parameter of nan; a COO matrix.
findings.fix: Digest and both Step builds are guarded; a non-finite parameter is left out.

findings.defect: A digest could differ for equal numbers: -0.0 against 0.0, rounding at nine decimals flipping on a 1e-12 jitter.
findings.scenario: A replay on another BLAS reported a false difference.

findings.defect: same_steps was None when the rerun had none but the original had some; trace returned the whole run with its steps; thousands of events per project; the route, the replay exit code and the real divergence were untested.
findings.scenario: make replay exited 0 for a rerun with no steps.
findings.fix: The comparison runs whenever the original has steps; trace returns a count; a start event is written only for units of work (a split, a transform, a fold), every step still ends with an event; tests for the route, the exit code and a real divergent replay.

outcome: Every stage run records its steps with their digests; a replay names the first step that differs; a decision traces to the steps that carry its numbers. Reviewed: 7 findings fixed (the granularity of imputation and encoding is a stated limit).
lessons: A recorder that is free when idle can be called from library code: no host needs to be threaded through the runner.
risks: The draft's cleaning actions are events of the draft, not steps of a run; a kind's machine takes one step.
A digest of a bounded sample cannot see a change in rows past the sample; the shape and the metric steps still can.
